title: Names on both lists
scenario: Two class lists. Which names are on both — each one once, in order?

intro.job: Two class lists. Which names are on both — each one once, in order?

idea.rule: Dedupe with a set, then sort — each shared name once, in order.
idea.detail: Two patterns chained: the set (015) keeps each name once; sorting (013) puts the shared names in order. The draft checks membership without deduping, so a name on both lists twice lands in the answer twice.

watch.code:
a, b = lists
shared = sorted(set(a) & set(b))
print(shared)

model_restatement: List the names on both lists, each once, in order.

clarify.question: What if a name appears twice on one list?
clarify.answer: It still counts once — the set keeps one copy.

clarify.question: Does the order matter?
clarify.answer: The answer prints sorted — a before b before c.

clarify.question: Does a name have to be on both lists?
clarify.answer: Yes — & keeps only what's in both.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Keep the names on both lists. Drop the duplicates. Sort them. Print them.

checkpoints.prompt: After the third name, what is shared?
On the print line, what is shared?
With the fix — after line 2, what is shared?

why_line: The draft walks list a and appends every match — 'ben' appears twice in a, so it lands in the answer twice.

explain.rule: Membership checks don't dedupe — `in` says yes every time it sees the name.
explain.bridge: How many times does 'ben' land in the answer — and what would keep it to once?

fix.rule: Intersect the sets, then sort: sorted(set(a) & set(b)).

walk.gloss: Unpack the pair into the two lists.
Keep only the names in both — the set drops the duplicate 'ben' — then sort.

contrast.right_note: each shared name once, in order

fix.recommended:
a, b = lists
shared = sorted(set(a) & set(b))
print(shared)

alternatives.note: Intersection as a method call — same shared names, same order.

hints: Which names appear more than once in the answer?
A list keeps duplicates — what doesn't?
shared = sorted(set(a) & set(b)) — then print it.

one_liner: Dedupe with a set, then sort — each shared name once, in order.
